claim: The FDA found that 100% of supplement manufacturing facilities inspected in India during FY2025 received noncompliance citations — all 10 of 10 inspected Indian sites failed — the worst result of any major supplement-producing country.
stance_target: Indian supplement manufacturers systematically fail GMP compliance, raising quality risk for Indian brands like Briyo
quoted_support: Countries that fared worst -- where all inspected facilities received citations of noncompliance -- were India, where all 10 of 10 inspected facilities received citations, as well as Japan (5 of 5), Brazil (3 of 3), New Zealand (2 of 2), Peru (2 of 2), and Switzerland (2 of 2).

claim: Nearly half (49.1%) of all 800 supplement manufacturing facilities inspected by the FDA in FY2025 received noncompliance letters for GMP violations, a slight improvement from 51% in FY2020.
stance_target: GMP compliance failures are widespread across the supplement manufacturing industry
quoted_support: ConsumerLab.com has obtained results of the FDA's inspections in Fiscal Year 2025 (October 1, 2024 - September 30, 2025) of 800 dietary supplement manufacturing facilities in the U.S. and abroad, showing that nearly half – 49.1% -- received letters indicating noncompliance with current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMPs).

claim: The most common GMP infractions found by FDA at supplement sites include: failing to establish product specifications for identity, purity, strength, and composition; lack of written quality control procedures; and incomplete batch records.
stance_target: What GMP compliance means for supplement quality assurance
scope_conditions: FDA supplement facility inspections, FY2020 detailed breakdown (most recent available)
quoted_support: In 2020, it informed ConsumerLab of a median of 4 infractions at facilities that received notices, of which the most common infractions were: not establishing product specifications for the identity, purity, strength, and/or composition of the finished dietary supplement; not establishing or following written procedures for quality control operations; not producing batch records which include the complete information relating to the production and control of each batch.

claim: ConsumerLab independently finds that about 1 in 5 (20%) supplements that it tests fail quality parameters, even though its testing focuses on more popular and established brands.
stance_target: Quality failure rates in supplements are significant even among mainstream brands
scope_conditions: ConsumerLab's own product reviews across all supplement categories
quoted_support: ConsumerLab finds that about one in five supplements in the U.S. and Canada that it tests in its product reviews do not meet quality parameters. Its testing tends to focus on more popular and established brands, guided by an annual survey of its readers' interests. Consequently, its overall findings tend to be better than those published by researchers focusing on general market or lesser-known brands.
numbers: 1 in 5 supplements fail quality parameters (ConsumerLab testing)
